location.ref: pad 'aisī lāl tujh binu kaunu karai …' (Ādi Granth, rāg Mārū)

paraphrase: Who but you, my Beloved, could do such a thing? Lord of the poor, you have set the royal canopy over my head — you make pure the one whose touch the world thinks polluting; you raise the low without fear of anyone. Nāmdev, Kabīr, Trilocan, Sadhnā and Sain crossed over; Ravidās says, hear, O sants: Hari does everything.
speaker: Ravidās

notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). Preserved in the Ādi Granth recension (Sikh scripture, cited as location only); page and rāg from memory, low confidence.

location.ref: pad 'begam purā sahar ko nāu …' (Ādi Granth, rāg Gauṛī)

paraphrase: The city's name is Begampura (the city without sorrow): there is no pain or anxiety there, no tax on goods, no fear, no fault, no decline; there is no second or third rank, all are one; it is ever settled and its king is steady; people go where they please, the palace is open to them; Ravidās the liberated tanner says: whoever is a citizen there is my friend.
speaker: Ravidās
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). Preserved in the Ādi Granth recension (Sikh scripture, cited as location only); page and rāg from memory, low confidence. (p. 345 on common report).

location.ref: pad 'dūdh ta bachrai thanahu biṭāriu …' (Ādi Granth, rāg Gūjrī)

paraphrase: The calf has sullied the milk in the udder, the bee the flower, the fish the water; what shall I offer you in worship? I offer you my body and mind and the guru's grace, and so I find the stainless Lord.
speaker: Ravidās
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). Preserved in the Ādi Granth recension (Sikh scripture, cited as location only); page and rāg from memory, low confidence.

location.ref: saying 'man cangā to kaṭhautī meṃ gaṅgā'

paraphrase: If the mind is pure, the Gaṅgā is in the leather-worker's bowl: purity is of the mind, not of the pilgrim place.
speaker: Ravidās
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). Proverb attached to the legend that the Gaṅgā appeared in Ravidās's tanning-water bowl; not in the Ādi Granth.

location.ref: pad 'merī jāti kuṭ bāṃḍhlā ḍhor ḍhovantā …' (Ādi Granth, rāg Malār)

paraphrase: My caste are the cutters and binders of leather who carry dead cattle around Banaras every day; now the chief brahmins bow before me — Ravidās your servant has taken refuge in your name.
speaker: Ravidās

location.ref: pad 'nāgar janāṃ merī jāti bikhiāt chamāraṃ …' (Ādi Granth, rāg Malār)

paraphrase: Townsfolk, my caste is known to be Camār; yet in my heart I keep the Lord's virtues; the wine made of Gaṅgā water is not taken by the sants, and the Gaṅgā's water poured into wine is not wine — so a low family does not stain the devotee.
speaker: Ravidās
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D

location.ref: pad 'prabhu jī tum candan ham pānī …' (Ādi Granth, rāg Sorath)

paraphrase: Lord, you are sandalwood and I am water; your fragrance has entered every limb; you are the cloud and I the peacock, you the moon and I the partridge; you are the lamp and I the wick, you the pearl and I the thread; you are the master and I the servant — such is Ravidās's devotion.
speaker: Ravidās
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D

paraphrase: No one is low because of birth; what makes a man low is the mud of low deeds.
speaker: Ravidās

paraphrase: Between you and me, me and you, what difference is there? As between gold and the bracelet, water and the wave. If I did not sin, how would you be called the purifier of sinners?
